outcome.technical:
WHAT CHANGED. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_clause_coverage.py: acceptance_reading now (i) counts an `Acceptance:` only where it opens a line (after indent and Markdown heading/quote/list/emphasis marks) or opens a sentence, never inside a code fence (_markers, _fenced_spans); each marker's body runs to the next marker and ends at the first heading line outside a fence (_body); with several markers the one holding a numbered list is read when exactly one does, else the last; a bold marker's closing asterisks are dropped. (ii) `(n)` opens an item only at the body start or after whitespace (`(?<!\S)`). When both numbered shapes yield items, the one whose first item opens earlier is read and the other's count is kept. Line-numbered items open only at the indent of the first `1.` (a sub-step on the marker's own line takes the marker line's indent); a `1.` at that indent opens a new item and sets `restart`. Both digit captures bounded to six digits. \r\n normalised. The reading dict now carries markers, markerLine, why, leadIn, other, restart. (iii) reading_line prints for every reading except a parenthesised list under one marker with no lead-in (is_plain), naming a second marker, the other shape's count, the left-out lead-in (quoted, shortened with textwrap.shorten) and a restart, and says the route: `held on the headless-writer route (executor.writerModel set): the writer answers each`. New reading_summary feeds the JSON key. audit-task.py: _say_acceptance_reading added to both dry-run reports (single and batch); optional `acceptanceReading` key added to add --json, add --dry-run --json, add --from-file --json (real and dry run, keyed by task id) and scope --description --json; key absent when the description holds no item; no existing key changed. scope has no --dry-run flag (audit-task.py VERB_FLAGS scope row), so 'under dry-run' applies to add only. audit-lookup.py _acceptance_named: names the marker's line when more than one marker exists, and says a restarted numbering. Documents: COMPATIBILITY.md Acceptance paragraph, CHANGELOG.md Changed entry (both sentences that named the executor/next submit), reference/manifest-conventions.md, commands/init.md, reference/verbs-in-full.md (the JSON key, after step 3 of the plan-writing call), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (_clause_coverage and audit-lookup sections only).

WHERE THE DESCRIPTION IS UNTRUE AGAINST THE CODE. Rule (i) says the marker counts ONLY where it opens a line. Taken literally that breaks the binding allow side: cc1, cs7, cs9b (tests/test__clause_coverage.py) and ar2/ar3 (tests/test_audit_task.py) use `Do it. Acceptance: (1) ...` with the marker mid-line, and the committed plans do too: count_sentence_markers.py under the scratchpad's sg1.24 directory prints `descriptions with a counted marker: 101; with one opening a sentence part-way along a line: 75`. So the implemented rule is: opens a line OR opens a sentence (after . ! ? plus optional closing quote/bracket/emphasis and whitespace). Every mention the description lists (inside a sentence, in backticks, in quotes, in a fence) is still excluded. Mutation row 'ALLOW the marker counted only at a line start' turns cc1, cs7, cr2b and the cc* verdict cases red, which is the measurement behind this choice.

BEFORE/AFTER OVER THE COMMITTED PLANS (probe_plans.py, HEAD reader exported with git show vs the tree's): `files read: 1240; descriptions holding the marker text: 102; changed reading: 1; reading line silent<->said: 1`. Changed reading: docs/audit/phases/P142.json P142.37-6yq (cancelled): HEAD read 1 parenthesised item from a QUOTED marker inside a sentence (`contradicts task clause 'Acceptance: (1) time python3 ...'`); now no item. Defended: the marker is a quotation of another task's clause, exactly rule (i)'s excluded class; the task is cancelled, so nothing is owed. Line change: SG1.24-ukq (this task) - reading unchanged (8 parenthesised items), now prints `2 Acceptance markers ... read the one on line 27 (the last)` because its description shows an example list headed by a line-opening `Acceptance:`; both bodies hold a numbered list, so the last (the real one) is taken.

PROBES. probe_before_after.py (review/d/probe_clauses.py CASES + probe_lints.py block 4, HEAD vs tree) - output in the scratchpad's sg1.24/probe_before_after.out. Rows the description calls wrong, now right: two markers last in prose (HEAD unnumbered ['list above.'] -> parenthesised ['a passes', ...]); backticks and quoted sentence (unnumbered fragment -> no item); code block (unnumbered ['none ```'] -> line-numbered 2 items, a, b...); bold empty (['**'] -> none); marker then heading (['## Notes...'] -> none); block 4a (parenthesised 1 item, silent -> line-numbered 3 items); block 4b (parenthesised ['when refused...'] -> unnumbered whole text); paren inside md list (-> 3 items, line names the parenthesised shape's 1 item); nested sublist (-> 2 items, sub-steps inside item 1); list then prose section (last item ends at the heading); restart (1 item -> 3 items, line says restart); big number (CRASH -> no exception). Rows that were right read the same items (substeps in paren item, lowercase, heading no colon, criteria, starts at 0/2, wrapped number, cr only, 1.) form, tab, unicode, superscript, bullet, quoted list); their reading line changed only in the route wording, plus a lead-in note for starts at 0, preamble and paren 1 in prose only. The code-block row's last item still runs into the fenced example (the rule ends an item at a heading, not at a fence) - left as the rule states. add_probe.py drove the orchestrator's seven descriptions through add under plain, --dry-run and --json (output sg1.24/add_probe.out): the plain parenthesised list prints nothing in plain and dry-run, and carries {shape: parenthesised, items: 2, line: ''} in JSON; every other one prints the same line in all three.

MUTATIONS. sg1.24/mutations.py, throwaway copy, anchor asserted once per row, __pycache__ purged, restored byte for byte: `MUTATIONS ALL CAUGHT`, exit 0; output in sg1.24/mutations.out. Rows asked for: rfind over the whole text (cr1 cr2 cr3 cr5 red), fence exclusion removed (cr3), paren glued to a word (cr6b), reading line silent on two shapes (cr6c), indent rule removed (cr9), each digit bound removed (cr11), dry-run line removed single and batch (ar8), JSON key removed single/scope (ar9 ar10) and batch (ar11). Allow twins: plain paren list prints (cs9b cr6e ar3 ar6 red), paren item with numbered sub-steps split (cr6e cs4 red), key written for no item (ar10), single-marker line in closing line (wp17b). Plus heading cut, last-always, lead-in silent, restart, route wording, closing-line marker line.

The five named suites through the sweep: `5/5 files ok, 2845 cases`, exit 0, both before and after the lint fix below. measure-context --gate: exit 0 `GATE OK`. ruff `All checks passed!`, vermin 3.8 clean. The orchestrator's gate without --record (run-test-gate.py ... --task SG1.24-ukq) went RED once on my code: tests/test__output_lints.py te11 and ln1 flagged _clause_coverage.py:296 (a length check beside a slice in the quote-shortening helper). DEPENDANTS. drive-phase.py's two callers of the check: file_writer_return (drive-phase.py:4607-4611) and aside_gap (drive-phase.py:5255-5261) - code unchanged; both call task_clauses on the task's CURRENT description at filing time. A TASK IN PROGRESS on the headless-writer route whose item list the new reader changes: the writer's closing line was composed at session start (audit-lookup.py compose_writer_prompt, writer_closing_line call at :1479) from the old numbering, and the drive checks the answer against the new one. If the new list is longer, the extra clause numbers are gaps (`no-answer`) -> clauses_uncovered (drive-phase.py:4410-4425): while a resume round is left the decision is `clauses-uncovered-writer`, which resumes the session with resume_text naming each uncovered clause's number and words, so the writer can answer; once rounds are spent it is plain `clauses-uncovered` (a fresh retry). If the new list is shorter, the writer's surplus keys land in `unknown`, never a gap. A key whose number now names a different clause is still judged only on whether its cited path is in the diff (check never reads clause meaning), so a renumbering can pass a clause on an answer written for another one - stated, not fixed here. On the committed plans no in-progress task's reading changed (probe above). audit-lookup.py writer closing line and task_clauses: changed only in _acceptance_named (marker line, restart); task_clauses unchanged; wp17 still green, wp17b added. tests/test_audit_lookup.py closing-line cases: green (206/206). tests/test__refs.py pins quoting commands/init.md (ia cases: _IA_CLAUSE, _IA_ROUTE, `_clause_coverage.py` inside the bullet) kept and green; no pin quotes the manifest-conventions passage. tools/measure-context.py --gate: exit 0 (init.md is not a measured entry). OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER (not built, as instructed): the two routes differ. On the headless-writer route (executor.writerModel set) the writer is asked for an answer per clause and the drive checks it at filing; on the executor subagent route submit reads no clause and the executor's brief asks for none (compose_executor_brief, audit-lookup.py:665, has no clause line; agents/audit-executor.md never mentions Acceptance). Whether submit should run the clause check, and the executor brief carry the closing line, is the owner's call.
